summary: Preserves not-found responses for missing historic process instances after tenant and runtime authorization.
userImpact: Looking up a process ID that does not exist on the selected engine returns a generic not-found response instead of an internal error.

changes: Historic process-instance detail returns HTTP 404 for a typed engine GET 404; other typed failures retain their existing status and safe diagnostics.
OpenAPI documents the engine selector, typed error envelopes and both tenant-prefixed and verified-host compatibility paths for historic process-instance detail.

security: Authentication, engine tenancy, runtime-resource permissions and private engine transport remain mandatory.
Unknown errors and upstream response bodies are not disclosed; upstream authorization or availability failures are not classified as not found.

customerDocumentation.reason: Technical HTTP error classification; no changed administrator setup or user workflow.

knownLimitations: A published image remains immutable; deployments require a newly qualified forward release.
rollback: Revert the application image; there are no data changes to undo.
validation: Route tests cover engine-wide and resource-aware missing instances, foreign-engine rejection, typed upstream authorization/availability failures, lookalike errors and safe unknown-error responses.
PostgreSQL integration uses real application authentication, an owned bounded HTTP engine peer, exact endpoint policy and an actual engine HTTP 404.
Source-to-generated OpenAPI regression checks discover the historic detail registration and both router mounts, and verify required selectors, success and error schemas.
Protected candidate, current exact-image security, database portability and live post-upgrade denial checks remain required.
